title: Web Workers for heavy computation
when: The page freezes during a long calculation (parsing big files, image processing, search indexing, simulations).
prompt:
Goal: Heavy work runs in a module worker with progress, cancellation and errors reported to a responsive page.
Steps:
1. new Worker(new URL("./worker.js", import.meta.url), { type: "module" }).
2. Protocol: in { id, type: "start" | "cancel", payload }, out { id, type: "progress" | "result" | "error", data }.
3. A call(type, payload) wrapper returns a promise matched by id and rejects on error messages and worker.onerror.
4. In the worker, process in chunks, post progress every few hundred ms, check a cancelled flag between chunks.
5. Transfer big binaries instead of copying: postMessage(msg, [buffer]).
6. No DOM in the worker; terminate() it when no longer needed or for a hard cancel.
Quality bar:
- The interface stays responsive and shows progress.
- Worker errors reach the page with a readable message.
- Pure functions shared by page and worker live in one module.
Pitfalls:
- Posting huge objects back and forth each step.
- Using window or document inside the worker.
- Loading from file://, where workers fail; serve the folder.
Verify:
- [ ] Worker created with type module.
- [ ] Messages carry ids and types.
- [ ] onerror handled.
- [ ] Progress shown in an aria-live region.
Output: js/worker.js, js/worker-client.js (promise wrapper) and the page code calling it.

examples.input: the page freezes while it parses my 80 MB CSV
examples.output: parse in a module worker in 1 MB chunks, progress messages, cancel button, result posted back
